facts.text: A vehicle dynamics model is a set of equations that predicts how a machine moves, slows, turns, leans and pitches in response to brake, drive and steering inputs.
facts.quote: A vehicle dynamics model is a set of equations that predicts how a machine moves, slows, turns, leans and pitches in response to brake, drive and steering inputs.

facts.text: A point-mass vehicle dynamics model uses speed, deceleration and grade to predict straight-line stopping distance well, but cannot represent tipping or swinging.
facts.quote: It knows speed, deceleration and grade, and it predicts stopping distance well in a straight line. It cannot say anything about tipping or swinging, because a dot has no shape.

facts.text: The booklet reports rigid vehicle dynamics models with 3 to 8 degrees of freedom for articulated loaders that “reasonably agree” with scaled-model tests.
facts.quote: The booklet reports rigid models of 3 to 8 degrees of freedom for articulated loaders that "reasonably agree" with scaled-model tests [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Multibody vehicle dynamics models show roll, articulation and load transfer in detail, but require many parameters.
facts.quote: It shows roll, articulation and load transfer in detail, but it needs many parameters.

facts.text: A wheel-loader digging model had to use a physically implausible tire-ground friction coefficient of 2.0 to match measurements, according to the booklet.
facts.quote: The booklet notes a wheel-loader digging model that had to use a tire-ground friction coefficient of 2.0, a physically implausible value, to match measurements [Chapter 8].

facts.text: The booklet separates a small, conservative vehicle dynamics model used at runtime to decide when to brake from a richer offline model used to challenge the runtime model.
facts.quote: The booklet separates a small, conservative model used at runtime to decide when to brake from a richer offline model used to challenge it.

facts.text: Multibody vehicle dynamics models are needed where lateral stability, articulation, individual axle or track loading, or deformable terrain matters; elsewhere, a calibrated point-mass model is enough.
facts.quote: Multibody models are needed where lateral stability, articulation, individual axle or track loading or deformable terrain matters; elsewhere a calibrated point-mass model is enough

facts.text: A simulation round robin showed that complex vehicle models can disagree more than simple vehicle models.
facts.quote: a simulation round robin showed that complex vehicle models can disagree more than simple ones [Chapter 8].
